invariant: fixed_mask should have some observable effect, or should refuse loudly if semantically meaningless for this surface
method: differential probe: score() called with fixed_mask=all-ones vs all-zeros on an identical sequences_to_score input, titanix CPU
summary: fixed_mask has zero measurable effect on score() output (bit-identical mean/std/sum). Silently accepted, does nothing -- same shape as prior audit's F002/F005 (silently discarded field). Semantics may legitimately be N/A for score() (a given sequence is already fully 'fixed' by definition), but the field is not rejected or documented as inert -- a caller has no signal.
blast: high (a caller who thinks fixed_mask restricts which positions contribute to the returned score gets no error and a wrong mental model of what was computed)
silence: high (bit-identical output, no warning, no exception)
closure_evidence: loud refusal (F002/F005-shaped, not real wiring): runner.score() now raises NotImplementedError naming fixed_mask when it has any nonzero entries, pointing at runner.sample as the surface that honours it. Chose refusal over guessing at masking semantics inside score.py's NLL path, which has documented history of nats-level leakage bugs from unverified changes (see score.py:145-172 comments). Regression tests in tests/host/test_fixed_mask_score_jacobian_guard.py; full tests/host/ suite re-run on titanix after the fix (387 passed, 10 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 new failures).

invariant: a batched Protein's chain_ids/chain_index must let a caller recover each residue's TRUE chain letter for the structure it actually came from
method: differential probe while scoping G2 (chains_to_design): two 2-residue-per-chain synthetic PDBs, chains {A,B} and {C,D} respectively (same chain COUNT, different LETTERS), batched together via create_protein_dataset(batch_size=2); resolved row 1's first residue's chain letter via chain_ids[chain_index[1][0]] and compared to ground truth. Second arm: heterogeneous chain COUNT (2 vs 1) in one batch.
summary: pad_and_collate_proteins's stacking of Protein silently keeps only structure 0's chain_ids list and reuses it for every row in the batch when chain counts match -- row 1's true chain 'C' resolves as 'A'. This is silent, wrong-answer corruption, not a crash: no exception, no warning, valid-shaped output. The heterogeneous-count case at least crashes loudly (jax pytree structure ValueError) rather than silently succeeding. Root cause is in proxide (external dependency), not aminx-authored code -- discovered before any aminx consumer read chain_ids, so currently dormant/latent, not yet biting a live path.
blast: would be high for chains_to_design specifically (G2): any multi-structure batch (batch_size>1) mixing PDBs with different native chain lettering would silently apply the WRONG chain design/fix assignment to every structure but the first.
silence: high (same-count case): no exception, no warning, plausible-shaped output.
recommended_next_step: Full fix scoping filed as .praxia/docs/specs/260826_proxide-chain-ids-batch-collision-fix.md: root cause pinned to proxide/ops/transforms.py::_stack_padded_proteins treating chain_ids (a list) as a jax.tree_util.tree_map-mappable container; 3 ranked candidate fixes (special-case assembly in proxide; pytree_node=False + explicit list-of-lists; aminx-side stopgap workaround) with acceptance criteria tied to re-running this finding's own probe. Do not implement chains_to_design against batched chain_ids until one of these lands and is re-verified the same way FA1 verified fixed_mask.

invariant: score() must be invariant to padding length within PADDING_TOLERANCE_NATS=1e-9
verdict: FAIL (as measured); assessed as a tolerance-calibration bug, not a real masking leak
evidence: titanix run log /tmp/aminx_slow_parity_run.log (ephemeral, not repo-committed); real run on CUDA backend, proteinmpnn_v_48_020, 1ubq.pdb chain A, pad lengths (76,96,128,192)
method: real differential run: same structure/sequence/key, only max_length varies, across 4 pad lengths on titanix's CUDA backend
summary: Measured spread 2.384e-07 nats vs the test's own 1e-9 tolerance -- about 7 orders of magnitude below the 0.0160-nat effect size the test's own docstring cites as the real masking-leak signature it exists to catch. The test's own comment already anticipates this exact failure mode ('a different XLA backend could reorder the masked sum enough to move the last ulp') -- this is the first time this test has run on a CUDA backend rather than CPU, and float32 non-associative summation reordering from different padded array shapes is a well-known, unavoidable source of ULP-level drift, independent of masking correctness. Confirmed identical (pre-existing) at the pre-G1 baseline commit.
blast: low -- no real masking-correctness issue implied by this measurement
silence: none -- test fails loud, just miscalibrated for this backend
recommended_next_step: Loosen PADDING_TOLERANCE_NATS for GPU/CUDA backends (e.g. backend-aware tolerance, or bump to ~1e-6), or gate the ultra-tight bound to CPU-only runs. Do not treat the current failure as a masking regression signal without first re-measuring with a much looser bound to confirm the spread stays flat rather than growing with a real leak's signature.

invariant: aminx's ligand feature extraction (V, E, Y_nodes, Y_edges) matches the pinned PyTorch LigandMPNN reference within specified tolerances when ligand_mpnn_use_side_chain_context=False
verdict: FAIL, root-caused as stale test vs. an intentional, documented fix -- not a live correctness bug
evidence: reference source dauparas/LigandMPNN@26ec57ac976ade5379920dbd43c7f97a91cf82de model_utils.py (ProteinFeaturesLigand.forward, ~lines 1247-1283: atom_context_num nearest-neighbor reorder is INSIDE `if self.use_side_chains:`) vs aminx src/aminx/model/ligand_features.py (~lines 383-396: same reorder runs unconditionally); commit a90ad4f9
method: code-level comparison: cloned the pinned reference commit fresh and read ProteinFeaturesLigand.forward directly, compared against aminx's __call__ and its own git history (git log -S on the unconditional-select comment)
summary: aminx's a90ad4f9 (2026-06-09, 'top_k atom selection now runs unconditionally, not only in use_side_chains path') fixed a real production OOM: 155 ligand atoms flowing into _y_edges_coords_to_embed with use_side_chains=False pre-allocated ~20GiB, causing RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED on every GPU tier including H200 and crashing real tev_design SLURM jobs (15645692, 15646995, 15721680). That fix made the atom_context_num-nearest-atom selection run for EVERY call, whereas the pinned reference only performs this reorder inside its own `use_side_chains=True` branch. For this test's use_side_chain_context=False config, aminx now returns the SAME underlying ligand-atom feature values as the reference but distance-sorted rather than in raw input order, so a flat row-by-row Pearson correlation reads low (0.677... vs required 0.85) despite both frameworks encoding the same physical atoms -- confirmed by the printed arrays: v_jax[0,i+1,:] matches v_pt[0,i,:] almost exactly for i=0,1,2, the signature of a clean reordering, not corrupted values. The a90ad4f9 commit never touched this test.
blast: none identified against real model correctness -- the model's ligand cross-attention is designed to be permutation-symmetric over the atom_context_num axis; blast is purely to this test's ability to catch a REAL future regression until it's updated
recommended_next_step: Update the test to compare order-invariant (e.g. sort both frameworks' V/Y_nodes rows by a stable key -- ligand atom coordinate or type -- before diffing), or construct both the PyTorch and JAX models with the SAME use_side_chains=True config for this specific comparison so both sides perform the same reorder. Do not revert a90ad4f9 -- it fixes a real, previously-crashing production OOM.

invariant: an SC-on model with sidechain reveal fully masked to zero (chain_mask=1 everywhere) must produce logits indistinguishable (<1e-5 max|delta|) from an SC-off model built from the same PRNG seed
verdict: FAIL -- real, small residual leak; mechanism hypothesized from code tracing but not confirmed via print-level tracing
evidence: titanix run log /tmp/aminx_slow_parity_run.log (ephemeral, not repo-committed): delta_reveal=0.073000 (confirms SC gating works when actually revealed -- rules out the mechanism being entirely broken), delta_sc_vs_off=3.536e-04 (required <1e-5)
method: real run on titanix CUDA backend, synthetic small PrxteinLigandMPNN model (_small_ligand_model, use_sc True/False from the SAME jax.random.PRNGKey(10)); ruled out a PRNG-divergence explanation by reading PrxteinLigandMPNN.__init__ directly -- ligand_mpnn_use_side_chain_context is a pure static runtime-behavior flag that does not change how many sub-keys are split before constructing the shared (non-SC) layers, so both configs genuinely share identical weights
summary: After a90ad4f9's unconditional top-k fix, the SC-on model's masked-out-reveal path concatenates 32 additional (ligand_mask=0, but real-valued-coordinate) pseudo-atoms from atom_37[:,5:,:] before the shared top-k select, yielding a 16-atom selection (k_y=min(16,36)); the SC-off model never concatenates them and gets only a 4-atom selection (k_y=min(16,4), the real ligand_atoms count in the test fixture). The two configurations therefore feed differently-SHAPED ligand-context arrays through the rest of the network even though the true SC contribution should be exactly zero when fully masked. This is a plausible mechanism for the leak (a reduction such as LayerNorm over norm_nodes/norm_y_nodes/norm_y_edges computing statistics across the full 16-atom axis, including the zero-masked-but-nonzero-valued padded rows, rather than only the true unmasked atoms) but was not pinned down via print-level tracing on titanix -- flagged as a real, if minor, correctness concern distinct from FT1's backend noise.
blast: low-medium -- affects sidechain-conditioning numerical precision specifically when sidechain reveal is masked to (near-)zero for some but not all residues in a batch; does not appear to break the qualitative SC-on/SC-off distinction itself (0.073 real signal remains ~200x the leak size)
recommended_next_step: Trace whether norm_nodes/norm_y_nodes/norm_y_edges (or another non-attention-masked reduction in ProteinFeaturesLigand.__call__) computes statistics over the full atom_context_num=16 axis including zero-masked-but-nonzero-valued padded rows, rather than only the true, ligand_mask=1 atoms. Compare against how the pinned reference's own use_side_chains=True path (which has the SAME concatenation-then-select shape, since it's where this logic originated) handles the identical all-zero-mask edge case -- if the reference has the same residual, this may be an inherited, accepted limitation rather than an aminx-introduced one.
